<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918380_theRebbe_210" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918380_theRebbe_210__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening with the date and Torah portion.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Acharei-Kedoshim,</t>
    <t s="2">13 Iyar 5721*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Specifies the time and place of the discourse.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">– In the morning before prayer,</t>
    <t s="1">in his room –</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains the Midrashic question on the verse "Kedoshim Tihyu" and the resolution in Likkutei Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Speak to the entire assembly of the children of Israel, etc., 'You shall be holy, for I am holy.'"1</t>
    <t s="1">And it is brought in the Midrash:2</t>
    <t s="2">"One might think [you could be] like Me,</t>
    <t s="3">therefore the verse teaches 'for I am holy'—</t>
    <t s="4">My holiness is above your holiness."</t>
    <t s="5">And it needs to be understood:3</t>
    <t s="6">How is it even possible to have a mere supposition that they could be like Me?</t>
    <t s="7">And superficially, one could say,</t>
    <t s="8">that the reason for the supposition "one might think [you could be] like Me"</t>
    <t s="9">(even though a created being is incomparable to the Creator)</t>
    <t s="10">is,</t>
    <t s="11">because from the wording of the verse "You shall be holy, for I am holy"</t>
    <t s="12">(where "for I am holy" is the reason and explanation for "You shall be holy")</t>
    <t s="13">it implies,</t>
    <t s="14">that the command "You shall be holy" means that the holiness of Israel must be similar to His holiness—"one might think [you could be] like Me."</t>
    <t s="15">[And one could explain this,</t>
    <t s="16">since Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one,4</t>
    <t s="17">therefore Israel are connected to all matters that are above.]</t>
    <t s="18">But based on this, it needs to be understood</t>
    <t s="19">(on the other hand)</t>
    <t s="20">[regarding] the conclusion of the Midrash, "My holiness is above your holiness"—</t>
    <t s="21">how does this align with the wording of the verse "for I am holy"?</t>
    <t s="22">And it is explained in Likkutei Torah:5</t>
    <t s="23">that "your holiness" is the holiness drawn down through an arousal from below</t>
    <t s="24">(the performance of the mitzvot),</t>
    <t s="25">and "My holiness that is above your holiness" is a most elevated holiness that no arousal from below</t>
    <t s="26">(of the performance of the mitzvot)</t>
    <t s="27">reaches there,</t>
    <t s="28">and it is drawn down through teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="29">And explanation is needed:</t>
    <t s="30">After all, teshuvah is also the service of man,</t>
    <t s="31">an arousal from below,</t>
    <t s="32">so why is it called "My holiness that is above your holiness"?</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
